# Parkinson's disease — lifestyle and supportive care

## Concept packs

- [Run-level pack: Lifestyle and supportive care](https://llmsx.org/tree/parkinson-s-disease-lifestyle-and-supportive-care-diet-and-nutrition-caffeine-falls-and-home-safety-daily-living-cbt-and-cognitive-training-palliative-care-care-partners-and-care-models/): Run-level pack covering diet and nutrition, caffeine, falls and home safety, daily living, CBT and cognitive training
- [Caffeine, smoking, nicotine and alcohol associations with PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/caffeine-smoking-nicotine-and-alcohol-associations-with-pd/): Caffeine, smoking, nicotine and alcohol require separate interpretations for PD incidence and treatment after diagnosis
- [Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/care-partner-support-and-caregiver-burden-in-pd/): Care partners provide emotional and practical support in PD while facing risks to their own health, social lives and finances
- [CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/cbt-mindfulness-and-cognitive-training-in-pd/): PD-adapted CBT addresses mood and anxiety through cognitive and behavioral coping skills
- [Diet and nutrition in PD: Mediterranean, MIND, protein redistribution, ketogenic](https://llmsx.org/tree/diet-and-nutrition-in-pd-mediterranean-mind-protein-redistribution-ketogenic/): Mediterranean and MIND patterns are plausible supportive dietary approaches in Parkinson’s disease, but observational associations cannot establish slower progression
- [Fall prevention, home safety and mobility aids in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/fall-prevention-home-safety-and-mobility-aids-in-pd/): Exercise evidence is strongest for mild-to-moderate PD; improvements in balance or freezing do not invariably translate into fewer falls
- [Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living](https://llmsx.org/tree/living-well-with-pd-driving-work-travel-and-daily-living/): The Parkinson’s Foundation recommends assessing driving in light of symptoms and medication effects, considering workplace adaptations, and planning medication access and rest when traveling
- [Multidisciplinary care models and telemedicine in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/multidisciplinary-care-models-and-telemedicine-in-pd/): Remote examinations have limits, and digital exclusion can disproportionately affect people with more advanced PD
- [Palliative and advance care planning in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/palliative-and-advance-care-planning-in-pd/): Palliative care in PD supports quality of life, symptom relief and planning throughout illness

## Top sources, live-checked 2026-11-27

- [parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management (8 claims in this run)](https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/activities-daily-living/home-safety): Bathroom safety guidance recommends properly anchored grab bars, seated bathing options, better lighting and clear routes
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5595275 (7 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5595275/): Randomized PD telemedicine studies support reduced travel burden and convenient specialist follow-up; these access benefits should be evaluated separately from changes in clinical outcomes
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842 (7 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042842/): The 2020 trial did not demonstrate a significant between-group reduction in healthcare use; the authors cautioned that relevant events were few
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10802092 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10802092/): Psychoeducation and other caregiver support interventions are promising, but reliable long-term burden reduction is not established across programs
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7282876 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7282876/): PD-adapted CBT can improve depressive and anxiety symptoms compared with usual care or other control conditions
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9739738 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9739738/): The MIND/Mediterranean observational association has limited generalizability: the Fox cohort was predominantly white, wealthy and US-based
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6175383 (4 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6175383/): The ketogenic pilot reported exacerbated tremor or rigidity as the most common ketogenic-group adverse effect
- [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38320207 (4 claims in this run)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38320207/): In a one-year randomized trial in early PD, transdermal nicotine did not slow progression
